To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genes associated with phenotypical plasticity evolve at elevated rates in fire ants, and genes associated with caste evolution evolve rapidly in lineages that lack castes.
genes associated with phenotypes that are produced via phenotypic plastic mechanisms evolve rapidly in the absence of caste evolution.
genes associated with phenotypes that exhibit phenotypic plastic in S. invicata and A. mellifera have elevated rates of protein evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary history of the genes associated with phenotypes that vary with the environment and with the evolution of phenotypes that vary between individuals of a species.
the evolution of the genetic basis of phenotypic diversity.
how organisms adaptively respond and evolve to their environments and how the evolution of alternative phenotypes is associated with changes in the underlying genetic architecture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evolution of phenotypical plasticity is not the cause of the rapid evolution of genes associated to it, but rather the relaxed selection that occurs during the process of evolution of phenotypical traits is the cause of the evolution of genes.

genes evolving under relaxed selection can readily evolve new patterns of expression that facilitate the production of alternate phenotypes, and that this is an important mechanism in the evolution of phenotypes.
the evolution of phenotypes is a complex phenomenon that is not easily explained by simple models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
relaxed selective constraint is a precursor to evolution of phenotypically plastic traits.
genes associated with plastic traits evolve at a rapid rate in the fire ant, and that the evolutionary origin of these plastic traits may be linked to the evolution of genes under relaxed selection.
genes associated with phenotypes that exhibit plasticity evolve at a rapid rate.

relaxed selective constraint is a key precursor to the evolution phenotypic plasticities.
